purpose: Fixed list of program-level questions with explicit probabilities. Intended as the reward target for a redesigned autoresearch loop: a cycle counts as progress only if it changes at least one entry by at least `minimum_reportable_shift`. Probabilities are the external auditor's estimates on 2026-09-03; they are beliefs, not evidence, and must never be edited retroactively. Append a new event to `history` on every change.

rules.no_belief_may_be_moved_by_a_gate_failure: A failed preregistered gate moves `p_gate_passes_for_mechanism`, never `p_principle_true`, unless the gate's sensitivity has been measured on a positive control (B01).

confidence_vocabulary.gate_fail_confidence: confidence that a preregistered conjunction failed for a specific mechanism on a specific cohort
confidence_vocabulary.mechanism_false_posterior: probability that the exact mechanism has no useful effect in the tested class
confidence_vocabulary.principle_false_posterior: probability that the general principle has no useful effect at any feasible scale

beliefs.question: The current G1 gate conjunction would admit a known-good learned system (e.g. a small GPU transformer or SSM on a task where its advantage over PPM/CTW is established) at matched budget.
beliefs.why_now: No positive control was ever run through the gates in 99 experiments. Gates require simultaneously source-identical, cross-family, adversarial, R16 full-cost Pareto and frozen-ablation gain. The only transformer (CAL-20260901-0001) trained for 0.68 s.
beliefs.what_would_raise: A preregistered positive-control run in which a small transformer/SSM passes the gates on a byte-level text task.
beliefs.what_would_lower: The same positive control fails the gates despite known capability advantage.
beliefs.priority: highest: every other belief's update rule depends on this

beliefs.question: Operation counts and bytes touched, as used in every NEXTAI Pareto front, are a monotone predictor of measured GPU/CPU latency and energy across the algorithm classes compared (pointer-chasing classical vs dense parallel learned).
beliefs.why_now: CAL-20260901-0001: small transformer 2.9e11 work units in 0.48 s vs PPM 9.9e7 work units in 1.72 s; misprediction of roughly four orders of magnitude in the direction that favours classical controls.
beliefs.what_would_raise: A regression of measured time on ops per algorithm class with high R^2 across all existing controls.
beliefs.what_would_lower: More calibration points showing class-dependent inversions.

beliefs.question: RC2 as observed ('a classical sufficient statistic dominates the learned candidate at full cost') survives when cost is measured on hardware rather than counted as operations.
beliefs.why_now: RC2 is the most replicated pattern (~40 experiments) but every instance used op counts; B02 implies the cost axis may be inverted for exactly the classical controls that won.
beliefs.what_would_raise: Re-measuring 10 representative RC2 comparisons on GPU+CPU and finding the classical control still cheaper at matched quality.
beliefs.what_would_lower: The same re-measurement showing learned candidates cheaper in wall time on parallel hardware.

beliefs.question: The WT recurrent-residual gain (EXP-20260831-0006/0007) is caused by learned recurrent state rather than by slot-local RLS alone.
beliefs.why_now: Replicated, full-cost Pareto-nondominated, H96 extrapolation, but the plan never ran a recurrence-off/RLS-on ablation; the analysis itself names DMDc/VAR+RLS as a complete classical explanation. The cross-family quick (EXP-20260831-0008) does not discriminate this question.
beliefs.what_would_raise: Source-identical recurrence-off ablation loses the H96 margin; DMDc/VAR+RLS control does not match it.
beliefs.what_would_lower: RLS-only or DMDc+RLS matches the candidate at lower measured cost.

beliefs.question: An observation-learned recurrent/stack state can extrapolate systematically beyond training depth on a real (non-synthetic-generator) sequence task.
beliefs.why_now: EXP-20260901-0041/0042: 144/144 exact spans on a hash-disjoint Python-source corpus at depths 3-5 from training depth <=2, three seeds, ablations at 0. EXP-20260901-0044 tested a different operation and does not lower this belief. Task is still a 7-symbol delimiter projection of real code.
beliefs.what_would_raise: Same signature on a second, non-delimiter real sequence task with a matched small transformer failing to extrapolate.
beliefs.what_would_lower: Failure to replicate on any second real task; or a matched transformer extrapolating equally well at lower measured cost.

beliefs.question: The learned pushdown mechanism (HYP-0050) is a reusable operator that transfers to a different operation inside the same grammar without retraining.
beliefs.why_now: EXP-20260901-0044: 0/144 on inverse push reconstruction. This is a valid negative for the reusable-operator claim; it is not a negative for B05.
beliefs.what_would_raise: A bidirectional variant preregistered as a new mechanism succeeding on both operations.

beliefs.question: A single source-identical learner with frozen constants can transfer useful representation across >=3 anonymised, heterogeneous world families (the L2/L3 cross-family claim as operationalised in NEXTAI).
beliefs.why_now: Fourteen cross-family-capable hypotheses, zero L1/L2/L3 survivors (cycle 256). Consistent across synthetic four-family and real three-family cohorts. Caveat: anonymisation and zero-padding destroyed channel semantics, so this is evidence about the operationalisation as much as about transfer.
beliefs.what_would_raise: Transfer under a natural, non-privileged relation between observations (cycle 238 'relation-marked experience') in three real families.
beliefs.what_would_lower: Already low; further negatives add little.

beliefs.question: The cross-family source-identical requirement is a necessary condition for an LLM successor (as opposed to a NEXTAI methodological preference).
beliefs.why_now: Not present in the original manifest; introduced 2026-08-30 12:22. A dense LLM is not source-identical across anonymised physical sensor families either.
beliefs.what_would_raise: An argument that capability/cost advantage cannot exist without such transfer.
beliefs.what_would_lower: A system-first prototype showing a cost-slope advantage on one real task class without cross-family transfer.

beliefs.question: Near-zero knowledge-size query slope (dC/dK ~ 0) is by itself informative evidence for a better computational principle.
beliefs.why_now: Every indexed control achieves it; RC5 shows locality savings are downstream of having the correct address/state. This is one of the program's most robust findings.

beliefs.question: The advantage of a dynamically structured learned system over a dense autoregressive model, if it exists, appears only as an interaction of components (memory x representation x routing x local update x compilation), not in any isolated primitive.
beliefs.why_now: 58 isolated primitives failed while three isolated signatures (recurrent depth extrapolation, slot-local update, exact index with K-independent access) are individually real. No system with more than one principle was ever built (cycle 256 explicitly forbade it).
beliefs.what_would_raise: A system-first prototype combining the three signatures beats matched transformer on a cost-vs-K slope while each single-component ablation does not.
beliefs.what_would_lower: The combined prototype shows no signature beyond its best single component.

beliefs.question: The R1/R4/R16 reuse horizon is a realistic amortisation boundary for an LLM-successor candidate.
beliefs.why_now: EXP-20260901-0036 crossover extrapolates to R~50-55; EXP-0033 to thousands of queries. Deployed language systems answer 1e6-1e9 queries per learned artifact.
beliefs.what_would_raise: An argument that discovery must be re-paid per task at deployment.

beliefs.question: Closed-generator synthetic micro-worlds as used in NEXTAI can, in principle, exhibit a learned advantage over the strongest classical control at full cost.
beliefs.why_now: Cycles 239-242: the agent could not construct a world where relations carry information unavailable to a degree-2 ridge or spectral control. Every generator has a computable sufficient statistic by construction.
beliefs.what_would_raise: A synthetic world with a preregistered proof that no polynomial-time classical statistic recovers the target while a learner does.

beliefs.question: Signatures found on NEXTAI micro-worlds (depth extrapolation, local update, warm reuse) transfer to any language-like task.
beliefs.why_now: Untested. Zero contact with language, planning or code as a task in 99 experiments. Prior unchanged by the program.
beliefs.what_would_raise: A minimal real capability benchmark (byte/token text with K-scaled facts and 1-4 step composition) reproducing at least one signature.

beliefs.question: The 'conditional information-boundary exhaustion' conclusion (cycle 261) holds at the scale of models and compute relevant to the grand objective.
beliefs.why_now: Derived from 58 hypotheses tested as 1-seed quicks of hand-coded learners (width 16-32, 180 s CPU, K<=32). Cycle 237 itself assigns <0.20 to extrapolation to LLM scale.
beliefs.what_would_raise: The same failure taxonomy reproduced with gradient-trained candidates of >=1e6 parameters on GPU at K>=1e4.
beliefs.what_would_lower: Any positive from B04, B05, B10 at that scale.

beliefs.question: The current autoresearch loop (AGENTS.md + program.md rules as of cycle 282) produces net positive expected information gain per cycle.
beliefs.why_now: Cycles 248-282: ~35 consecutive no-scoring cycles, each ending with 0.995 confidence and no belief change; 'exact next action' rule produces an unbounded literature chain.
beliefs.what_would_raise: A redesigned loop that reports a belief-shift >= minimum_reportable_shift in at least 1 of 3 cycles.

beliefs.question: The grand objective (materially better capability per unit of end-to-end inference cost than dense autoregressive LLMs, via a dynamically structured learned system) is achievable at some scale.
beliefs.why_now: Unchanged. No experiment in the ledger operates at a scale, on a task, or with a cost model that bears on this question. Beliefs B01-B15 explain why.
beliefs.what_would_raise: B10 success trigger: matched capability, measured GPU cost slope vs K lower than transformer on 3 scales, 3 seeds, 2 task classes, R* < 1e3.
beliefs.what_would_lower: Section W stop criteria all satisfied after gate calibration.
